title: Phylogenetic tree as a Wikipedia diagram type
dek: Rooted/unrooted, topology versus lengths, Newick. The sampling-model likelihood stays on stats-trees.
story: Wikipedia's phylogenetic tree page is a diagram type: a graph of recency of common ancestry. Cladograms ignore lengths; phylograms use branch lengths; chronograms map lengths to time under a clock.

stats-trees already treats the tree as a sampling model (Markov process, Felsenstein pruning). This card is the encyclopedia diagram, plus Newick as a sibling card, so a pretty figure is not mistaken for a likelihood.
In TB, a tree is often a picture of lineage. Transmission inference is extra (stats-transmission-genomics).
deep: Rooting (outgroup, midpoint) is an extra claim.
Bootstrapping columns is not resampling independent outbreaks (stats-trees deep).
Recombination makes a single tree the wrong geometry.
Do not read a ladder as a march of progress.

visual.caption: Diagram type, then what the picture still is not. Likelihood lives one plate down.
